brief_title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Added to Dapagliflozin and Insulin Resistance in Type 2 Diabetes
official_title: Effect of Alpha-Lipoic Acid as Add-on Therapy to Dapagliflozin on Insulin Resistance and Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial

primary_outcomes.measure: Change in Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to test whether adding alpha-lipoic acid (ALA) to usual treatment with metformin and dapagliflozin improves insulin resistance in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does ALA 600 mg once daily for 12 weeks lower insulin resistance, measured by the Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR), more than a placebo?
* Does ALA also improve blood sugar control, body weight and waist size, blood pressure, and blood fats, and is it safe and well tolerated?

Participants will:

* Keep taking their usual metformin and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily without any change.
* Take one capsule every day for 12 weeks, either ALA 600 mg or a matching placebo (a capsule with no active ingredient), assigned by chance.
* Visit the clinic at the start, at week 6, and at week 12 for blood tests, body measurements, and safety checks.

Researchers will compare the ALA group with the placebo group to see if ALA lowers HOMA-IR more than placebo.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 30 to 70 years, either sex
* Established diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus
* HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.0% at screening
* On stable metformin plus dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for at least 3 months
* Able and willing to give written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Type 1 diabetes or secondary forms of diabetes
* Pregnancy, lactation, or planned pregnancy
* eGFR below 45 mL/min/1.73 m2
* Severe liver disease (Child-Pugh B or C)
* Acute coronary syndrome, stroke, or hospitalization for decompensated heart failure within the past 3 months
* Current or recent (within 4 weeks) use of alpha-lipoic acid, other high-dose antioxidant supplements, or insulin
* Known hypersensitivity to alpha-lipoic acid or placebo excipients
* Active malignancy or any condition that would prevent completing 12 weeks of follow-up
